environment: isolated disposable postgres:16 (127.0.0.1:15433) seeded read-only from production; all destructive ops confined to the container
result: FOUND THEN FIXED — end-to-end recovery failed on first run (3 defects), was repaired, and now passes end-to-end with deterministic reproduction.

findings.title: restore_database aborts on benign version-skew SET
findings.detail: Host pg tools are pg_dump/pg_restore 18.3 while the DB server (production and disposable) is 16.13. pg_dump 18 writes 'SET transaction_timeout = 0;' into every custom dump; restore_database runs 'pg_restore --clean --if-exists --no-owner --exit-on-error', and --exit-on-error makes the v16 server's 'unrecognized configuration parameter "transaction_timeout"' fatal. pg_restore exits 1 and restore_database raises CalledProcessError before any restore completes.
findings.validated_fix: Clean-slate restore: 'DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA public;' then 'pg_restore --no-owner' (no --clean, no --exit-on-error), then treat the run as successful only if stderr contains no errors other than benign 'unrecognized configuration parameter' SETs; otherwise raise. Verified in isolation: state reverted correctly with only the benign SET error.

findings.title: --clean cannot drop FK-referenced objects
findings.detail: Even ignoring transaction_timeout, 'pg_restore --clean' fails to DROP objects that are FK targets, e.g. 'cannot drop constraint users_pkey on table public.users because ... team_withdrawn_by_id_...fk_users_user_id on table public.team depends on it'. The dependency-ordered DROP is not CASCADE, so --clean leaves a partially-dropped schema.
findings.validated_fix: Same clean-slate DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE approach removes all FK-dependent objects first, eliminating these errors.

findings.title: Backup/code revision skew breaks the re-run
findings.detail: The re-run half (process_round with current code) fails with 'column team.participation_status does not exist'. The game-31 pre-resolution backups were written 2026-08-27T14:02Z, 34 minutes before migration 0060_team_participation_status was applied to production (2026-08-27T14:36Z). Restoring a pre-0060 snapshot and re-running current code queries a column the restored schema lacks. Compounding it, these manifests' code_revision field is EMPTY, so the command cannot even detect the skew.
findings.evidence: django_migrations 0060 applied 2026-08-27T14:36Z vs backup mtime 14:02Z; restored schema has no team.participation_status; manifest.code_revision is blank
findings.recommended_fix: Design decision required. Options: (a) fail-closed guard — refuse recovery unless manifest.code_revision equals the deployed GIT_REVISION (requires code_revision to be populated, which newer manifests do but these legacy ones do not); (b) run 'manage.py migrate' after restore to bring the schema to current code before re-run; (c) operational — during a frozen-code competition, backups and code share a revision, so this skew should not occur; still, the command should assert code_revision match and refuse otherwise.

note: Only the --dry-run path was exercised in prior verification, which stops before restore_database; that is why none of these were caught. The dry-run guards (maintenance-mode gate, confirm-token, >=10-char reason, instructor/admin actor, backup SHA-256 verification, durable JSONL intent audit) all work correctly.
isolation: Production was read-only (single pg_dump for seeding + read queries). No production database, service, or competition record was mutated by the drill. Disposable container gs-recovery-drill removed on completion.

fix.RD-01_RD-02: restore_database rewritten: DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE + CREATE SCHEMA (clean slate, no FK-drop ordering), then pg_restore --no-owner tolerating only benign cross-version SET failures (_restore_stderr_is_benign). Any other pg_restore error is fatal.
fix.RD-03: recover_competition_round now compares manifest.code_revision to the running resolve_code_revision() and refuses on mismatch (or empty) unless --allow-code-revision-mismatch. Revisions recorded in the durable intent audit.
fix.tests: core/tests/test_competition_hardening.py: added benign-classifier and code-revision-mismatch tests; updated dry-run test. Full suite 273 passed.

two_operator_sign_off: OUTSTANDING — human gate. The command records actor + reason in an immutable operator audit event and durable JSONL; a second operator must counter-sign per the runbook before a live recovery.
